selector_flow: CodeFlash[0x2570C] config0 = type1 + selector4 + zero padding
every H queue record references config0 and CryptoIf job0
CryptoIf begin stores the config pointer and finish forwards it through driver dispatch
command7 prepare copies config byte +4 into descriptor word4
command7 validates descriptor word4 < 15 and writes (word4 << 16) | 7 to ICUSCMD

command8_key_update.conclusion: the CPU forwards the authenticated 64-byte key-update package to ICU-S command 8; no fixed slot is selected by the CPU-side command descriptor, so target/key identity remains package-authenticated rather than a raw application key write

dataflash_raw_key_negative.boundary: The DataFlash dump and retained CAN oracle are contributor artifacts and are not proven same-runtime-epoch. The scan excludes an exact raw 16-byte candidate among the 23,277 tested windows; it does not exclude transformed/derived values or ICU-S-internal storage.
dataflash_raw_key_negative.interpretation: the committed exhaustive raw-window scan found zero candidate matches; this supports absence of an obvious CPU-visible raw key in the supplied DataFlash snapshot, not absence of derivation or protected hardware storage

evidence_boundary: Static CPU/application proof: all configured H SecOC queue records select one generated config/job, whose config is {type=1, selector=4}; CryptoIf forwards that object into the command-7 descriptor and ICUSCMD receives selector 4. No 16-byte raw key is passed through the command-7 CPU descriptor. This does not reveal undocumented ICU-S internal storage/derivation. DataFlash raw-key negatives retain their acquisition-epoch boundary.

shared_crypto_selection.conclusion: 00F, 0D7, and 0B6 share one ICU-S slot-4 authentication key selection; the firmware does not select three independent keys for these profiles

slot4_kat.meaning: disabled known-answer path independently corroborates job0/config type1/slot4 but places no constraint on the live slot-4 key value

static_storage_derivation_conclusion.best_static_model: mapped application SecOC init selects protected ICU-S slot 4; key value is opaque to command-7 CPU software and can be refreshed through authenticated ICU-S command-8 package handling
